title: What is an AI agent? A plain guide with small tasks
h1: what is an ai agent, in plain english?
description: See an AI agent at work on a small folder: how it differs from a chatbot, which tools it needs and what to tell it before it starts.
answer: **an ai agent does the steps you would otherwise do yourself.** give it a goal and suitable tools. it can read the material, act, see what happened and choose the next step. a chatbot tells you how to rename 200 files. an agent renames them. that's the whole difference, and also the risk.

review.by: lead agent: independent reviewer pass against seo/facts (4 reviewers), every finding applied, automated gate

og_line: a goal, some tools, and your limits.

sections.h: watch one small job instead of learning the jargon
sections.md:
**turn the folder you keep avoiding into a reading index.** each document gets a subject and a pointer back to its source.

the agent finds the files, reads them and groups them. an unrelated file or one it cannot open belongs in the result as a gap.

the failure to fear isn't a crash. it's a confident index that silently skipped half the folder.

sections.h: look at the tools behind the chat box
sections.md:
**ask which steps you still have to do yourself.** a chatbot can explain how to make the index. an agent with suitable tools can inspect the files and make it.

you might text either one. some chat products also have tools. the interface alone does not decide the difference.

the [agent versus chatbot comparison](/vs/ai-agent-vs-chatbot) goes further. for now, ask: can it reach the material and put the result where i need it?

sections.h: give it four things before it starts
sections.md:
**tell it what finished looks like.** 'help me get organised' leaves almost every decision open. try this brief instead.

- **goal:** make a reading index
- **material:** use this exact folder
- **boundary:** leave originals alone and report unreadable files
- **result:** group source names by subject in the chat

now you can compare the index with the folder. if a source is missing, ask why. keep the first result small enough to read in a few minutes.

**keep a bot that remembers the job for next time.** dusk is a desktop app for a small team you text like teammates. each bot has its own job and memory; you choose its name and ai.[^1]

dusk has no model of its own. it runs vendors' official command-line apps where your bots live. your chosen ai does the thinking.[^1][^2]

drop files into chat or use **attach files**. results appear there and live in the bot's folder or your chosen project folder.[^2] start with a folder. don't hand it your inbox on day one.

sections.h: access is one choice; repetition is another
sections.md:
**a useful first job can live inside one folder.** add an app when the task needs it, then look at the actions its connection gives the bot.

the [mcp guide](/guides/what-is-mcp) explains one way apps connect to tools. every extra permission should have a job to do.

in dusk, a routine repeats a job you describe once. local routines stop when the app closes or the computer sleeps.[^3] [scheduled ai tasks](/scheduled-ai-tasks) covers hosting. a finished reading index may never need a weekly schedule.

sections.h: read the result beside the source
sections.md:
**a source name beside each claim makes the review quicker.** compare dates, names and claims with the originals before passing the work on. a busy tool log tells you little about whether the answer is right.

keep the job small and the access narrow. when a run goes well, give it the next useful task.

before trying accounts or computer control, read the [safety guide](/guides/is-it-safe-to-let-ai-control-your-computer).

faq.q: what are people actually using ai agents for?
faq.a: **index documents, compare two files or review new entries in a tracker.** start with inputs you know, then compare the result with those sources.

faq.q: does an ai agent have to run all day?
faq.a: **no, one job is enough.** recurring work needs a schedule and a computer or hosted setup running when it is due.

faq.q: is an ai agent the same as a bot?
faq.a: **bot is the broader word.** look at a particular bot’s tools, access and instructions to understand what it can do.

sources.label: Metal docs: getting started and the ai

steps: choose two short files you can share
ask for one sentence about each, with its source name
tell it to leave originals alone
compare the answer with both files

worked.intro: an invented example with made-up people and files.
worked.before: nora has three project notes and a meeting in ten minutes. each file has a different title.
worked.after: the agent groups the three notes by subject and names their sources. one unreadable attachment appears under "could not open". nora knows what still needs her.

checklist.h: a first job you can review in minutes
items: the material is small and you know where it came from
the result has a clear shape
missing inputs must appear as gaps

mistakes.mistake: asking it to organise your whole life
mistakes.fix: choose one folder and one finished result.

mistakes.mistake: trusting the answer because tools ran
mistakes.fix: compare the sources it used with the material you gave it.

tip.text: your first agent job should be small enough that you can spot a wrong answer.
